title: Lodestar Financial - Ops activation briefing
next_steps: Redwood to send activation runbook and network checklist (Maya)
Schedule VPC peering and firewall review with Tim - propose slots next week
Customer to provide list of safe prompt sets for eval and monitoring (Evelyn)
SE to run pre-prod perf benchmark on 16k token path and share results
action_items: Maya - share activation runbook + pricing appendix by 2025-12-15
Daniel - run steady-state latency and cost estimate for expected qps by 2025-12-18
Tim - confirm network egress IPs and CIDR ranges by 2025-12-17

summary: Kickoff-style ops briefing to align on Lodestar's production activation path. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC connectivity, KMS/encryption, data retention and monitoring. Agreed immediate next steps: share runbook, schedule network prep, run benchmarks and gather security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for coming on. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE for Lodestar. We also have Daniel SE and Amira from CS. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Evelyn Ross: Evelyn here.
[00:10] Tim Nguyen: Tim, platform.
[00:12] Sara Brooks: Sara, CTO.
[00:14] Victor Hale: Victor - security.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Great. The goal today is a short ops activation briefing so we can lock the network and security checklist and get Daniel running the perf bench. We'll go 40 minutes and leave time for Qs.
[00:30] Daniel Cho: I can start with a high level of the deployment options, then we dig into questions.
[00:35] Daniel Cho: So two main paths - Hosted Redwood API which is fastest to start, managed keys, and predictable per-token pricing; or Dedicated capacity which gives you reserved GPU pools, private tenancy and lower marginal cost at scale. For Lodestar with sensitive financial PII, the common choice is Dedicated or Private with VPC peering.
[00:50] Tim Nguyen: Quick question - our security folks want to avoid egress to public IPs. Is VPC peering supported for dedicated?
[00:56] Daniel Cho: Yes, VPC peering is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. We also have an on-prem appliance option if you need air-gapped. There are a couple of things to confirm: CIDR ranges, expected egress IPs, and any proxy we need to route through.
[01:10] Victor Hale: For audit purposes we need KMS integration and customer-managed keys. Is CMK supported?
[01:14] Maya Patel: Short answer: yes. Redwood integrates with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) for private deployments and Dedicated can be configured with CMKs. We'll share the KMS setup doc.
[01:23] Victor Hale: Cool. Also SSO - we use Okta for SAML and SCIM.
[01:27] Amira Hassan: We support SAML/SSO provisioning and RBAC; we'll share the SAML metadata template.
[01:34] Sara Brooks: On the perf side, we have a ton of tail-latency sensitivity. We really need under 200ms 95th for short prompts, and can tolerate higher for long-generation. Can you run benchmarks with our sample payloads?
[01:44] Daniel Cho: Absolutely. We'll run two passes: short-path (prompt + 128 tokens) and long-path (8k-16k context). We did previously mention caching and batching knobs - for Lodestar we'd recommend prefix caching for repeated system instructions and a batching window tuned for your qps distribution.
[02:00] Tim Nguyen: How does continuous batching affect tail? We don't want batching to add jitter to latencies.
[02:04] Daniel Cho: Good point. Our runtime uses workload-aware batching which has strict latency SLO caps; you can configure max batching delay and set a strict route SLO that disables long batching for latency-sensitive routes.
[02:16] Evelyn Ross: Does Redwood keep KV cache in-memory on the GPU instances? We worry about cache warming and context reuse across requests.
[02:22] Daniel Cho: KV cache is managed by the runtime; for Dedicated we can pin warm instances and maintain long-lived KV to reduce cold-token overhead. There's a tradeoff with memory usage and cost.
[02:32] Victor Hale: On compliance, can we get logs for every API request with masked PII and retention controls?
[02:38] Amira Hassan: Yes, we provide request-level tracing and you can configure redaction rules. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We'll hand over the audit log schema.
[02:49] Sara Brooks: About rollout - we'd like a pilot that handles 10TPS, then gradual ramp. What does the typical timeline look like?
[02:56] Maya Patel: Pilot to canary to prod: typical is 2-4 weeks for pilot (integration + perf), 1-2 weeks for canary with monitoring and rollback hooks, then full prod ramp. Depends on your internal change windows.
[03:10] Tim Nguyen: Network-wise, what do you need from us now?
[03:12] Daniel Cho: We need CIDR peering details, any egress firewall rules, and whether you'll use NAT or direct peering. Also list of service accounts that need access to the console.
[03:24] Tim Nguyen: I can compile that. I'll also need the static IP ranges - do you have those?
[03:28] Amira Hassan: We'll share the static egress IP block in the runbook. Expect a small set of IP ranges per region.
[03:36] Evelyn Ross: For quality monitoring, can we hook in our evals? We run prompt sets nightly for regressions.
[03:40] Daniel Cho: Yes - Redwood Optimize supports scheduled evals and regression alerts. We can map your prompt sets and set thresholds; we'll attach a sample eval template.
[03:50] Victor Hale: Encryption in-transit; do you support mutual TLS for private endpoints?
[03:54] Daniel Cho: We support mTLS for Private deployments and mutual auth for Dedicated within a VPC. We'll include the cert rotation procedure.
[04:02] Sara Brooks: Licensing/pricing question — for Dedicated what's the typical commit vs overage model?
[04:06] Maya Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. We can do a pilot credit and then convert to a monthly commit with burst to hosted capacity if needed. I'll include a pricing appendix.
[04:17] Tim Nguyen: Any gotchas when switching from Hosted to Dedicated mid-pilot?
[04:21] Daniel Cho: Seamless routing is possible; we recommend pinning model versions and having a canary route. There may be quantization differences between variants; we'll test for quality delta.
[04:33] Evelyn Ross: Data residency — we require EU-region only for some workloads. Can you pin region?
[04:36] Maya Patel: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. We'll document region-specific IPs and latency expectations.
[04:46] Victor Hale: Ok final: we need SOC2 attestation, pen-test summary, and any subprocessor list.
[04:51] Amira Hassan: We'll send SOC2 cert, recent pen-test summary, and full subprocessor list. Expect that in the security bundle.
[04:59] Maya Patel: To summarize — action items: Maya will send activation runbook and pricing appendix; Daniel will run perf benchmarks with Lodestar's payloads; Tim will provide network CIDRs and confirm egress method; Victor will list security evidence questions. We'll aim for the network prep call next Wednesday. Anything else?
[05:18] Sara Brooks: Can we get a single doc with the minimal blockers for pilot go/no-go?
[05:21] Amira Hassan: Yes we'll produce a pilot readiness checklist and highlight must-have blockers.
[05:26] Evelyn Ross: Thanks, that's great.
[05:28] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the links. Links: activation runbook (https://redwood.app/runbooks/lodestar-activation), security bundle (https://redwood.app/security/lodestar-bundle), shared deck (https://redwood.app/decks/lodestar-kickoff).
[05:40] Meeting end.
